content: The following are professional descriptions of the references provided: 1. The 2014 UN-Habitat report discusses the integration of health considerations into urban and territorial planning, providing a comprehensive sourcebook for policymakers and planners. It emphasizes the importance of creating healthier cities to address the challenges of a rapidly changing world. 2. The WHO manifesto for a healthy recovery from COVID-19 outlines strategies to rebuild societies with a focus on health equity, sustainability, and resilience in the aftermath of the pandemic. 3. A guide on leveraging multi-level governance approaches highlights methods to promote health equity by addressing systemic barriers and fostering collaboration across different levels of government and sectors. 4. The Global Report on Urban Health emphasizes the need for equitable and healthier cities to achieve sustainable development, offering insights into urban health challenges and solutions. 5. The Gender Equality Action Plan (2014–2019) by UN-Habitat outlines strategies to promote gender equality in human settlements, focusing on inclusive urban development. 6. WHO’s initiative, More Active People for a Healthier World, promotes physical activity as a key component of global health improvement, with resources and tools to support implementation. 7. A toolkit for promoting physical activity in schools provides practical guidance for educators and policymakers to encourage active lifestyles among students. 8. The WHO Housing and Health Guidelines offer evidence-based recommendations to improve housing conditions and their impact on health outcomes. 9. A call to action from the Vienna Energy Forum emphasizes empowering women and youth to accelerate the transition to clean energy, highlighting the intersection of energy access and health. 10. A toolkit for clean household energy solutions provides resources to address indoor air pollution and its health impacts, particularly in low-resource settings. 11. A report on the physical environment as a determinant of adolescent health explores how environmental factors influence the well-being of young people. 12. The publication Don’t Pollute My Future. examines the impact of environmental factors on children’s health, advocating for stronger policies to protect vulnerable populations. 13. A global assessment by Prüss-Üstün et al. 14. UNICEF’s State of the World’s Sanitation report highlights global progress and challenges in achieving adequate sanitation, with a focus on equity and sustainability. 15. A WHO and UNICEF report underscores the importance of healthy and inclusive learning environments in schools, particularly in the context of COVID-19 recovery efforts. 16. WHO’s fact sheets on ambient (outdoor) air pollution and household air pollution provide detailed information on their health impacts and strategies for mitigation. 17. The 2012 report on endocrine-disrupting chemicals reviews the state of scientific knowledge on these substances and their potential health effects. 18. WHO’s guidance on chemicals and health offers tools and resources to address chemical risks and their impact on public health. 19. The GEO-6 for Youth report by the United Nations Environment Programme engages young people in addressing climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution. 20. The United Nations Environment Programme’s strategy for 2022–2025 outlines actions to tackle climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution, emphasizing sustainable development. 21. A joint UNICEF and WHO report on drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene in schools highlights the critical role of these services in promoting health and preventing disease, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. 22. The State of the World’s Hand Hygiene report calls for prioritizing hand hygiene in policy and practice to improve global health outcomes. 23. The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) framework provides a comprehensive agenda for achieving global sustainability by 2030, with specific targets and indicators. 24. The Global Strategy for Women’s, Children’s, and Adolescents’ Health (2016–2030) outlines a roadmap to improve health outcomes for these populations through targeted interventions. 25. A scoping review of adolescent health indicators identifies key metrics for monitoring and improving adolescent health globally. 26. Research by Azzopardi et al. tracks progress in adolescent health and well-being across 195 countries, using 12 headline indicators from 1990 to 2016. 27. The Countdown to 2030 initiative monitors progress toward universal health coverage for reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health, providing data-driven insights. 28. The Measuring Mental Health Among Adolescents at the Population Level (MMAP) initiative focuses on developing standardized tools to assess adolescent mental health. 29. 30. The DHS Program provides high-quality data to plan, monitor, and improve population, health, and nutrition programs globally. 31. UNICEF’s Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS) offer valuable data on the health and well-being of children and adolescents, supporting evidence-based decision-making. 32. WHO’s resources on noncommunicable disease surveillance and monitoring provide tools to track and address the global burden of these diseases. 33. The Health Behaviour in School-aged Children (HBSC) study examines the health and well-being of young people, offering insights into their behaviors and environments. 34. WHO’s Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) initiative supports countries in collecting and using data to improve health outcomes and accountability. 35. The WHO Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health and Ageing Data Portal provides easy access to global, regional, and national health data for these populations. 36. The Adolescent Data Portal and Youth Dashboard offer comprehensive data on adolescent and youth health, supporting targeted interventions and policies. 37. Research by Guthold et al. highlights the effectiveness of participatory approaches in developing school health interventions in low-resource settings. 38. The WHO publication Working Together for Health and Sustainable Development emphasizes the importance of collaboration across sectors to achieve health and sustainability goals. 39. The Handbook of Adolescent Development Research explores the impact of research on global policy, focusing on the unique needs of adolescents. 40. A multi-country study by Banati and Bacalso examines risk and protective factors for emotional and behavioral problems among early adolescents. 41. The Global Financing Facility (GFF) strategy review assesses progress in achieving health outcomes for women, children, and adolescents in lowand middle-income countries. 42. A global research agenda for adolescents living with HIV identifies priorities to improve their health and well-being, addressing unique challenges faced by this population. 43. The COVID-19 Research Prioritization Group outlines global research priorities for maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health in the context of the pandemic. 44. Research by Hindin et al. identifies priorities for adolescent sexual and reproductive health in lowand middle-income countries, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions. 45. Nagata et al. propose research priorities for eight key areas of adolescent health in lowand middle-income countries, addressing critical gaps in knowledge. 46. Research by Svanemyr et al. focuses on ending child marriage and supporting married girls, identifying key areas for intervention and policy development. 47. Rudan et al. provide guidelines for setting priorities in global child health research investments, using the CHNRI method to guide decision-making. 48. Santelli et al. discuss ethical considerations for obtaining informed consent when conducting research with adolescents, emphasizing the importance of inclusion and protection. 49. Guthold et al. evaluate the effectiveness of participatory approaches in developing school health interventions, using a cluster randomized controlled trial in low-resource cities. 50. The WHO publication Principles for Evaluation of Development Assistance provides guidelines for assessing the impact of health programs and interventions. These descriptions provide a detailed overview of the references, highlighting their relevance to health, sustainability, and development.
